Required claim: the level-one partition Fock space with residue c-r mod e, node weights and degree, and the e-regular/e-restricted naming. Used to fix the residue convention and the label classes. Open finding for the supplier's Step-3 author: the parenthetical 'e-restricted when no column has length e' is not the definition and must be corrected to lambda_a - lambda_{a+1} < e (no e equal column heights); the consumer does not use the gloss.

Required claim: i-nodes listed top to bottom, cancellation of a - above a +, normal/conormal nodes, good = topmost normal, cogood = bottommost conormal, with residue c-r. Used verbatim as the modular reading of the convention. Supplier is scaffolded on batch-22 (dependency_level 0), not yet authored.

Required claim: the i-nodes ordered by content (larger content = further right) and the exponents N^r_i, N^l_i with the good node as the minimiser. Used for the identification of the content order with the top-to-bottom order and for the transfer of the reading order. Open finding for the supplier's Step-3 author: the sentence 'the unique addable i-node minimizing N^r_i' and the bracket recipe give different nodes in general and neither is the Fock crystal operator (see the row on def-good-and-cogood-nodes-by-residue-signature-reduction); the consumer uses only the order and the exponent definitions.

Required claim: the reduced i-signature and the good/cogood extrema in the top-to-bottom reading. Used for the term-by-term mirror comparison with the Fock reading. Supplier is scaffolded on batch-22 (dependency_level 0), not yet authored.

Required claim: the Fock crystal with B(F) the partitions and arrows f~_i = plus the good i-node, e~_i = minus the cogood i-node, with the empty component the e-regular partitions. Used as the quantum side of the comparison and for the transport of the arrow rule. Supplier is scaffolded on batch-9 (dependency_level 19), not yet authored.

Required claim: the Fock good/cogood nodes by signature reduction. Used for the naming dictionary between the two readings. Open finding, recorded for the supplier's Step-3 author and for the batch-9 owner: the bracket recipe as scaffolded (order by increasing content, cancel pairs )(, good = leftmost uncancelled opening) computes the restricted reading and contradicts the Fock module action -- at lambda = (2,1), e = 3, i = 2 the word is )( and the rule returns no arrow, while the standard-vector action gives F_2|2,1> = |3,1>; the correct Fock rule is the column-decreasing (top-to-bottom) reading with cancellation of a + before a - and the last surviving + as the f~ node, first surviving - as the e~ node (see Fayers sec. 2 and sec. 4; Leclerc (38)-(39)). The consumer's statement uses the corrected rule and does not rely on the printed bracket sentence. The batch-9 crystal theorem's phrase 'the good i-node' must be read with this correction.

Required claim: the empty component is B(Lambda_0) and its complement in B(F) is non-empty, with the axiom-of-choice bookkeeping.
